header.name: Dairy_V1
header.full_name: Dairy plant V1: cheese and mesost
header.authors_and_contributors: Sophia Wallerand, Daniel Flórez-Orrego, Pullah Bhatnagar, Oktay Boztas, Dareen Dardor, EPFL IPESE research group
header.description: Cheese dairy whose whey is boiled down with part of the cream into mesost, a Scandinavian brown whey cheese. 28 thermal streams per 1 t/h of fresh milk.
header.references:
[1] Dardor, D., Flórez-Orrego, D., Terrier, C., Ribeiro Domingos, M.E., Platteau, C., da Silva, J.C., Lopez, M., Maréchal, F., ROSMOSE: A web-based decision support tool for the design and optimization of industrial and urban energy systems. Energy 304 (2024) 132182, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2024.132182;
[2] Ramírez, C.A., Patel, M., Blok, K., From fluid milk to milk powder: energy use and energy efficiency in the European dairy industry. Energy 31(12) (2006) 1984-2004, DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.energy.2005.10.014

units.unit_description: This unit processes 1 t/h of fresh milk into cream and cheese: reception, pasteurisation with regenerative heat exchange and cream separation, three-effect evaporation of the skimmed milk, cheese making and brining, cleaning in place and wastewater treatment. The whey is boiled down with part of the cream into mesost, a Scandinavian brown whey cheese. In the OSMOSE model, the heat streams are grouped by section into the units Pasteurisation, Evaporation, Cheese, CIP and Mesost, and the material flows and the electricity into the unit Plant_boundary, all at the scale CAPACITY.
units.connectors_description: The unit takes fresh milk, salt, water for brining and water for cleaning (CIP), and electricity, and delivers cream, cheese, mesost, mesost vapour (to CIP), evaporator condensate water, treated water discharge, CIP water discharge and wastewater sludge. The material flows close at 1,187.3 kg/h in and out.

units.heat_streams_description: 13 cold and 15 hot streams per 1 t/h of fresh milk, from the DWSIM dairy model of Bhatnagar, Flórez-Orrego, Boztas and Dardor and from Dardor et al. (2024). The evaporator is described effect by effect. Phase changes at constant temperature have a span of 0.1 K; the ΔTmin/2 contribution is 5 K for liquid streams and 2 K for boiling and condensing streams. Streams ending below about 20 °C need refrigeration unless another process stream absorbs their heat.
